title: Kernel affinity scorer + burst prefill probe for mixed-sku fleets (H100/L40S/A10)
creator: Priya Singh
description: Implement a lightweight runtime component (kernel affinity scorer) that computes a per-request affinity score to select among candidate microkernels and to decide whether to opportunistically prefill/batch on adjacent MIG slices or sibling GPUs. The scorer will combine model+request features (seq_len, prompt prefix entropy, model size), hardware state (MIG slice size, current SM clock headroom, thermal headroom, NVLink locality) and queueing signals (current inflight tokens, expected decode duration) to pick the best kernel variant and a prefill strategy. The goal is to reduce short-tail latency (p50/p95/p99 for small interactive chat requests) without increasing tail variability for throughput workloads. This ticket covers design, a low-overhead implementation, micro-benchmarks on H100/A10 mixed fleets, and a canary rollout path with telemetry gating.
acceptance_criteria: Affinity scorer implemented and compiled into runtime (feature-flagged)
End-to-end tests verifying correct kernel selection for at least 6 synthetic request shapes (short/long seq, sparse tokens)
Canary on 5% traffic for dedicated h100-a10 mixed queue showing >=6% p99 reduction for <64-token interactive workload without >3% regression in throughput tail for long-batch workloads
Dashboard with scoring breakdown, selected kernel id, and prefill decisions hooked into existing Grafana alerting
Fallback behavior tested: when telemetry unavailable or power headroom low, scorer yields safe default kernel and disables prefill
notes: Initial idea came from dev pairing session with infra team; draws on prior prefill heuristics but shifts decisioning earlier into request admission path.
Scorer must be deterministic and cheap: target <50us decision latency and <1% additional CPU utilization on serving nodes.
We will avoid any model-architecture-dependent ML in the scorer for now — use hand-tuned weighted features with an alpha blending factor that can be tuned from console.
Power/thermal tradeoff: aggressive prefill can improve p99 but increases average clock and power; include knob to cap prefill when thermal headroom < threshold.
implementation_steps: Spec: define feature vector, scoring function, and config knobs (weights, thresholds, prefill budget)
Telemetry: extend runtime telemetry to emit chosen kernel id, score components, and prefill decision per request
Runtime: implement scorer as feature-flagged module in request admission path; integrate with kernel selector interface
Prefill probe: add burst probe that attempts to warm KV cache on adjacent slice with budget-aware rate limiter
Bench: microbench single-node H100/A10 mixed MIG partitions with 100k synthetic chat requests, record p50/p95/p99 and power envelope
Canary: deploy to dedicated fleet (canary policy) with gradual ramp and automated rollback if alert triggers
experiments_and_results: Lab run 2026-03-04 on h100 (4xA100->simulated) and single A10: short-chat workload (<64 tokens) saw median latency -10%, p95 -8%, p99 -6% when scorer enabled with conservative prefill budget
Long-batch throughput test (512 tokens) showed <1.5% throughput regression in the worst case when prefill budget capped at 10% of cycles
Ablation: disabling NVLink locality in the score yields +4% p99 for islanded workloads; NVLink locality helps when multi-GPU attention offload is used
Power: aggressive prefill mode increased average node power ~12W (~3.5%) on H100 under mixed load — acceptable under current infra budgets but requires opt-in
tradeoffs_and_risks: Increased scheduling complexity may cause oscillations if prefill budget is not rate-limited — mitigation: tokenized leaky bucket and hysteresis on clock gating
Telemetry stream volume increases; must ensure ingestion pipeline scales or sample scores at 1/10 for high-throughput tenants
Edgecase: tiny prompts on heavily throttled MIG slices may get worse latency if scorer mis-estimates headroom — include safe-mode fallback
Operational: exposes additional knobs to SRE; require clear defaults and an auto-disable policy for overheating events
comments: 2026-02-26 Priya Singh: Drafted spec after benchmarking day. Opening ticket to track design + canary. Assigned to Alexei for implementation.

2026-03-02 Alexei Morozov: Implemented initial scorer prototype (flag runtime.kernel_affinity=true). Microbench harness in a local branch (github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/2241). Observed promising reductions on short-chat synthetic workload. Need to reduce scorer CPU cost.

2026-03-04 SRE review (Lina Martinez): Concern about power rise during aggressive prefill. Suggested cap prefill to 10% cycles and add thermal headroom check. Also requested alert on average node power delta >5W.
2026-03-07 Design review (Evan Zhao): UX should expose a 'conservative' preset and a 'latency-first' preset. Recommended adding a brief console tooltip explaining power vs latency tradeoff.
2026-03-10 Alexei Morozov: Integrated leaky-bucket rate limiter for prefill. Optimized scorer path to reduce branching; decision latency now ~28us on p99 in microbench.
2026-03-12 QA (Maya Patel): Added unit tests for deterministic scoring and a regression test verifying fallback when telemetry gaps occur. Preparing canary plan for next rollout window.
